newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro says 1996 hit by weaker metals, chems.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro says 1996 hit by weaker metals, chems.

text.p: Norway's largest listed company Norsk Hydro ASA on Monday attributed a 10 percent decline in 1996 operating profits to significantly lower earnings for light metals and petrochemicals.
The industrial giant said its oil and gas division showed a marked improvement in operating income for the year, while results for agriculture were slightly below the year-earlier period.
Norsk Hydro posted operating profits of 9.65 billion crowns for 1996 compared with 10.70 billion crowns a year ago.
The result included a charge of one billion crowns due to a downward revision of remaining oil and gas reserves in the North Sea Frigg area and for provisions for future abandonment costs.

Net profits of 6.20 billion crowns, against 7.15 billion, included a reduction in the provision for deferred taxes of 776 million crowns due to a change in the tax law for hydroelectric power plants in Norway.
"Excluding the effect of the change in tax law, net income would have been NOK 5,428 million. This was a decline of 24 percent compared with 1995," Hydro said in a statement.
"The reduction was principally due to lower prices for aluminium and petrochemical products, and a decrease in energy production."

Net income in the fourth quarter of 2.01 billion crowns was strongly influenced by the deferred tax effect of the change in the tax law. Excluding the tax effect, net income would have been 1.24 billion crowns, down 10 percent from the fourth quarter 1995.
Hydro said results for 1995 and 1996 were in line with its Hydro Plus programme launched in 1993 to increase operating income to 10 billion crowns.

"Hydro's 1996 result confirms that the company has lifted its rate of return to a new and more satisfying level," Egil Myklebust, Hydro's president and chief executive officer, said in the company's Profile newsletter.

"The primary goals of Hydro Plus...have essentially been reached two years in a row. That's very positive. On the other hand, the impact made by market fluctuations on the 1996 result shows us that we still need to improve our cost efficiency. Our fourth quarter results are a reminder of that," Myklebust said.
Hydro's share price fell sharply in early trade and at 0939 GMT stood 20 crowns off at 358.50 crowns in 91.1 million crowns of business.
